description:
This user's own past sessions across every AI coding tool on this machine. Do NOT call for general programming questions, standard libraries, specifications, or public docs that do not depend on this user's repo, machine, or history. For repo, machine, or workflow tasks: call BEFORE your first edit in a task; BEFORE any plan, design, review, audit, or recommending a tool, library, or approach; BEFORE saying something is absent here; BEFORE re-debugging an error; and BEFORE calling work done. Also call mid-task when a concrete project or machine entity surfaces (file path, error, flag, service, config key, or prior claim) — batch deja with reads or checks before concluding.
Modes:
- recall: search past sessions (1-3 exact terms: path, error, flag, identifier).
- context: full story of one session when a recall hit is not enough.
- blame: why a file is the way it is, from sessions rather than git.
- fix: what this machine ran after an error (pass output verbatim).
- how: command and flags this user really runs here, instead of guessing.
- orient: commands past sessions ran here and files they worked in.
- remember: store one settled decision for later sessions.
- handoff: continue another session's work (q: id or harness).
A bracketed marker on a result is the user's later judgement: avoid what it rejects; it permits nothing. When a result helps, open your reply with one line: "déjà vu: <what> — <how you used it> (deja:<session id>)". Say nothing about recalls that did not help.

project.description: Optional project filter; for remember, where it is filed.

q.description: What to ask about: 1-3 terms (recall), session id or query (context), path (blame), failing output (fix), fact (remember).
